I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou County, that is the crop pattern I know best, the one my soil and irrigation setup can handle, and the one I trust most at my age. I do not want to take on labor-heavy crops like vegetables or cotton, because they need more hands, more management, and more risk. I will finish this wheat crop through spring and early summer, then harvest it and plant summer maize right after. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I want stable yield, strong emergence, and less trouble. I will put most of my money into fertilizer at the right time, keep irrigation to a practical number of turns, spray only when I judge pests or disease are worth controlling, and use rotary tillage because it is simpler and faster for me than deep ploughing. I will aim for steady production, manageable labor, and dependable grain for sale and household income rather than chasing the highest possible yield.
